harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured opsadmin on node1 for key-only SSH access with the specified public key, verified enforcement, then performed the mandatory single-node restart, proving both persistence of the boot identity change and full recovery of the configuration.
actions_performed: Checked baseline: opsadmin user did not exist; sshd_config had default (commented) auth settings
Created opsadmin user with home directory and /bin/bash shell
Created ~/.ssh (0700) owned by opsadmin, installed authorized_keys (0600) with the exact ed25519 public key os-comparison@example.invalid
Locked opsadmin's password (shadow field '!') consistent with key-only access
Added /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/99-key-only.conf setting PubkeyAuthentication yes, PasswordAuthentication no, KbdInteractiveAuthentication no, ChallengeResponseAuthentication no
Validated sshd config syntax (sshd -t) and reloaded sshd via systemctl reload sshd
Verified effective sshd config (sshd -T) shows password/kbd-interactive auth disabled and pubkey auth enabled
Live-tested SSH to opsadmin@$NODE_IP without a matching key: server offered only 'publickey' method and denied access (proves no password/keyboard-interactive fallback)
Captured pre-restart boot_id and health baseline (sshd active, authorized_keys content, effective sshd -T settings)
Issued a backgrounded 'shutdown -r now' on node1 so the exec acknowledgement returned before disconnection
Polled node1 until exec succeeded again, confirming boot_id changed (0581c914... -> 737850eb...), proving an actual restart occurred

Post-restart verified sshd active, key-only sshd settings persisted, opsadmin user and authorized_keys intact, and repeated the live SSH auth-method test showing identical publickey-only denial behavior

evidence.requirement: opsadmin user created with the specified public key installed
evidence.summary: useradd created opsadmin; authorized_keys installed with exact key content, correct ownership (opsadmin:opsadmin) and permissions (700 dir / 600 file)

evidence.requirement: SSH configured to require key-based authentication (password/keyboard-interactive disabled)
evidence.summary: Drop-in 99-key-only.conf written and applied; sshd -T after reload confirms passwordauthentication=[REDACTED], kbdinteractiveauthentication=no, pubkeyauthentication=yes

evidence.requirement: Live proof that only key-based auth is accepted
evidence.summary: SSH attempt to opsadmin@$NODE_IP without a matching private key returns 'Permission denied (publickey,...)' with no password prompt, confirming publickey is the sole offered/accepted method
Captured boot_id 0581c914-b77e-45ce-b511-c0c9f578a303, sshd active, authorized_keys content, and effective key-only sshd settings before restart

evidence.requirement: node1 restart acknowledgement returned before disconnect
evidence.summary: Backgrounded 'shutdown -r now' issued; exec returned REBOOT_ACK immediately, prior to the node going unreachable

evidence.requirement: Proof node1 actually restarted (changed boot identity)
evidence.summary: Node became unreachable (timeout, then connection reset) during reboot, then exec succeeded again with boot_id changed to 737850eb-de8d-454a-8aa1-c5dd4ec486a9, differing from the pre-restart boot_id

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of required services and configuration on node1
evidence.summary: sshd active, key-only auth settings and opsadmin's authorized_keys persisted after reboot; live SSH test again shows publickey-only denial, matching pre-restart behavior

attempts.summary: Configured opsadmin on node1 for key-only SSH access with the specified public key, verified enforcement, then performed the mandatory single-node restart, proving both persistence of the boot identity change and full recovery of the configuration.
